citations.quote:
Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel $c\subset a\otimes b$, let $i_{ab}^c:c\to a\otimes b$ be the
standard unit-vector isometric inclusion. Since the multiplicity space is
$V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$, its orthonormal basis vector is
the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided tensor category and let $u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$
be its Drinfeld isomorphism. For a natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity
functor, put

$$\psi_X:=u_X\theta_X.$$

Then $\psi$ is a pivotal structure if and only if $\theta$ is a twist.

Let $(-)^{\vee\vee}$ be the monoidal endofunctor of
[[thm-the-double-dual-is-a-monoidal-functor]].

A **pivotal structure** on a rigid monoidal category is an isomorphism of
monoidal functors

$$a:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^{\vee\vee}.$$

Equivalently, it is a natural family of isomorphisms
$a_X:X\xrightarrow{\sim}X^{\vee\vee}$ such that

$$a_{X\otimes Y}=a_X\otimes a_Y,\qquad a_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$$

after transporting along the monoidal structure of the double-dual functor.

Assume chosen left duals $X^\vee$ and $Y^\vee$ of objects $X$ and $Y$. For a
morphism $f:X\to Y$, its **left dual morphism**

$$f^\vee:Y^\vee\to X^\vee$$

is the composite

$$Y^\vee\xrightarrow{\rho^{-1}}Y^\vee\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1\otimes\operatorname{coev}_X}Y^\vee\otimes(X\otimes X^\vee)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}}(Y^\vee\otimes X)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{(1\otimes f)\otimes1}(Y^\vee\otimes Y)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_Y\otimes1}\mathbf 1\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\lambda}X^\vee.$$

Equivalently, $f^\vee$ is the unique morphism making the transpose squares with
evaluation and coevaluation commute. The right dual of a morphism is defined by
the mirrored formula once right duals are chosen.

Fix a rigid monoidal category with chosen left duals. For a morphism
$a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, the **left categorical trace** of $a$ is the endomorphism
of the unit

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(a):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X}X\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{a\otimes1_{X^\vee}}X^{\vee\vee}\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1.$$

For a morphism $b:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$, the **right categorical trace** of $b$ is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(b):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes b}X^\vee\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X}\mathbf 1.$$

So a bare endomorphism $X\to X$ is not yet an input to categorical trace; one
first needs a comparison between $X$ and a double dual.

Let $a$ be a pivotal structure on a rigid monoidal category. The **dimension of
an object $X$ relative to $a$** is

$$\dim_a(X):=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a_X)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1).$$

The subscript is part of the notation: changing the pivotal structure changes
the morphism whose trace is being taken, so the resulting dimension can change
as well.

Following EGNO, a **spherical structure** is a pivotal structure $a$ on a tensor
category such that

$$\dim_a(X)=\dim_a(X^\vee)$$

for every object $X$.

A **spherical category** is a tensor category equipped with a spherical
structure.

1.1 The positive real choices give $u^2+u=1$, $v^2=u$ and $u^2+v^2=1$, so the real symmetric block $F$ satisfies $F^\dagger F=F^2=I$. All scalar unit-gauge blocks are unitary. The phases $x,y$ have modulus one and $x=y^2$ exactly. To fix the root and sign without a numerical cosine approximation, $y^5=-1$ and $y\ne-1$ give $y^4-y^3+y^2-y+1=0$. Dividing by $y^2$ shows that $z=y+y^{-1}$ satisfies $z^2-z-1=0$. Since $z=2\cos(3\pi/5)<0$, it is $(1-\sqrt5)/2=-u$. Thus $y^2+uy+1=0$, with this chosen root, not its conjugate. The object-level braiding has eigenvalues $x^{-1},y^{-1}$, so inverse-precomposition gives exactly the stated pullback eigenvalues $x,y$. [F1, F4, F5, given, algebra]

2.3 The unit object is self-dual. The $\mathbf1$ summand of $\tau\otimes\tau$ gives an isometric inclusion $i:\mathbf1\to\tau\otimes\tau$; set $\operatorname{coev}=\sqrt\phi\,i$ and $\operatorname{ev}=\sqrt\phi\,i^\dagger$. In either zig-zag composite for $\tau$, the only intermediate channel is $\mathbf1$, so its scalar is $\sqrt\phi\sqrt\phi\,F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}[\mathbf1,\mathbf1]=\phi u=1$. The opposite zig-zag uses $F^{-1}=F$ from step 1.1 and has the same coefficient. Hence $\tau$ is self-dual; duality extends to finite direct sums, so the category is rigid. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

derivations.claim: For a finite direct sum $A=\bigoplus_{s,p}s$, let $I_{s,p}:s\to A$ be its fixed copy inclusions. Set $A^\vee=A$ and $h_A=\sum_{s,p}(I_{s,p}\otimes I_{s,p})h_s$, $e_A=h_A^\dagger$, where $h_{\mathbf1}=e_{\mathbf1}=\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$. Each cross-copy term in a snake vanishes, and each diagonal term is the simple snake from [F1], so these are duality maps on every finite sum. In the evaluation mate identity, the coefficient for copies $p,q$ of simple $s$ is $\sqrt{d_s}(f_s)_{pq}$ on one side and $\sqrt{d_s}(f_s^\vee)_{qp}$ on the other, where $d_{\mathbf1}=1$ and $d_\tau=\phi$ denote the cup/cap normalization constants at this stage. Thus $f_s^\vee=f_s^{\mathsf T}$, without complex conjugation, by uniqueness of mates. The double dual is therefore literally the identity on objects and morphisms. This alone does not yet establish its tensor comparison. The empty sum uses the unique zero maps and satisfies the same identities.

Define $\theta_A$ to be the identity on every unit copy and $x\operatorname{id}_\tau$ on every $\tau$ copy. These central scalar blocks are natural for arbitrary morphism matrices. Of the four ordered simple pairs, the three containing a unit satisfy the twist law by the strict unit gauge. On $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$ its two channel equations are $$x^2(x^{-1})^2=1,\qquad x^2(y^{-1})^2=x,$$ the latter because $x=y^2$. Tensoring copy inclusions and then inserting the simple channel inclusions exhausts every finite direct sum, so these equations prove the twist law on all objects, including zero. Also $\theta_{\mathbf1}=1$. Duality is block transpose by step 1.1, so $\theta_A^\vee=\theta_{A^\vee}$; hence this twist is ribbon.

In [F2]'s typed formula for $\mathfrak u_\tau$, the map $\operatorname{id}_\tau\otimes h_\tau$ starts in the right tree $\tau\otimes(\tau\otimes\tau)$, with its last pair in the vacuum channel. Apply $\alpha^{-1}$ to reach $(\tau\otimes\tau)\otimes\tau$, then $c_{\tau,\tau}\otimes\operatorname{id}_\tau$, and finally $e_\tau\otimes\operatorname{id}_\tau$. Let $R_{\mathbf1}=\operatorname{id}_\tau\otimes w$ be the right-vacuum inclusion, and let $L_{\mathbf1}=w\otimes\operatorname{id}_\tau,L_\tau$ be the orthonormal left-tree inclusions. The object block is $F^{-1}=F$, so $\alpha^{-1}R_{\mathbf1}=uL_{\mathbf1}+vL_\tau$. The middle braiding gives $ux^{-1}L_{\mathbf1}+vy^{-1}L_\tau$. The final cap is on this same first pair: $L_{\mathbf1}^\dagger L_{\mathbf1}=1$ and $L_{\mathbf1}^\dagger L_\tau=0$. With $e_0=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}$, the complete two-channel compression is therefore $$\mathfrak u_\tau=\phi e_0^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(x^{-1},y^{-1})F e_0\operatorname{id}_\tau=\phi(ux^{-1}+0\cdot vy^{-1})\operatorname{id}_\tau=x^{-1}\operatorname{id}_\tau,\qquad \mathfrak u_{\mathbf1}=\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}.$$ Naturality at all copy inclusions gives precisely these scalar blocks on every finite sum. No dagger conjugation of $x$ or extra F move is inserted.

By steps 2.1–2.2 and [F3], $j=\mathfrak u\theta$ is a monoidal natural isomorphism, and its blocks are all identity. To check the tensor comparison explicitly, the three unit-input cases in [F2]'s relation give $d_{a,b}=1$. In the two $\tau\tau$ channels that relation gives $$d_{\tau,\tau}|_{\mathbf1}=\frac{1\cdot x^{-2}}{x^{-2}}=1,\qquad d_{\tau,\tau}|_\tau=\frac{x^{-1}y^{-2}}{x^{-2}}=xy^{-2}=1.$$ Thus the four ordered simple pairs, including both nonunit root channels, have identity comparison. Naturality at all tensor products of copy inclusions extends this to every finite sum; the unit comparison is identity in the strict unit gauge. This proves the required pivotal monoidality rather than merely objectwise double-dual isomorphisms.

Since $A^\vee=A$ and $j_A=1$, the left closure is $e_A(f\otimes1)h_A$ and the right closure is $e_A(1\otimes f)h_A$. Orthogonal copy inclusions kill all off-diagonal terms; the diagonal term for a copy of $s$ is $d_s(f_s)_{pp}$ on either side. Summing proves both displayed trace formulas. In particular $\dim_j(A)=m_1+\phi m_\tau=\dim_j(A^\vee)$, so [F4] makes $j$ spherical with simple dimensions $1,\phi>0$. For $f=g^\dagger g$, the formula is a sum of these positive weights times squared absolute matrix entries, and vanishes only for $g=0$. The zero object has trace and dimension zero.

If $j'$ is another pivotal structure, $\gamma=j^{-1}j'$ is a monoidal natural automorphism of the identity. Naturality at copy inclusions makes it scalar $1$ on unit copies and $t\ne0$ on $\tau$ copies. Monoidality on the unit and $\tau$ summands of $\tau\otimes\tau$ gives respectively $t^2=1$ and $t^2=t$. Hence $t=1$, and all components of $\gamma$ are identity. This proves uniqueness and the asserted canonical positive spherical structure, with every trace and ribbon convention already established.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 supplies unique zero cups/caps and step 3.1 the empty tensor comparison; step 4.1 gives trace0 for the empty direct sum.
Every zero-dimensional multiplicity block and zero object is included; step4.1 gives weighted trace0 and faithful positivity vanishing only for the zero morphism.
The unit cup, cap, twist and Drinfeld component are identity; steps2.1 and3.1 exhaust all three ordered pairs containing the unit.
A sum may contain zero copies of either simple; the diagonal formulas and copy-inclusion exhaustion remain valid without assuming both types occur.
Step2.2 types the right-vacuum inclusion, one inverse associator, the first-pair braiding and left-vacuum cap; both ττ channel coefficients are retained before the second is killed by orthogonality.
No arbitrary nonempty-family choice is made: simple bases and direct-sum copy inclusions are fixed in the explicit model; all sums are finite.
No iff classification is asserted. Existence and monoidality are proved in3.1, and uniqueness by the two separate scalar equations in4.2.
No converse hypothesis is imported;4.2 begins with an actual second pivotal structure and proves its equality on every copy.

Exact types, one-F compression, inverse object-braiding orientation, x=y², monoidal comparison, transpose duals, both weighted traces, zero and uniqueness are supplied. No general unitary-to-positive-pivotal theorem is a premise. Root focused proof adjudication/current certification and all native independent later review are still owed; this open marker does not claim native acceptance.
